physics_goals.quote: designed to measure the scale of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of matter over a larger volume than the combined efforts of all previous spectroscopic surveys of large scale structure
physics_goals.value: Measure the scale of baryon acoustic oscillations in the clustering of matter over a larger volume than all previous spectroscopic surveys, with galaxies to z<0.7 and the Lyman-alpha forest at 2.15<z<3.5.

summary.plain: The Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey, part of SDSS-III, measured the distances to over a million galaxies and to distant quasars. It used the faint ripples left in the universe by sound waves in the early cosmos as a ruler to track cosmic expansion.
summary.technical: SDSS-III survey on the 2.5-m telescope at Apache Point with two new 1000-fibre BOSS spectrographs (R~2000, 360–1000 nm). Dark-time observations fall 2009 to spring 2014: 1.5 million luminous galaxies to z=0.7 over 10,000 deg² and Lyman-alpha forest spectra of 160,000 quasars at 2.2<z<3, measuring BAO distances to 1% (z=0.3, 0.55).
